description: Single-panel scatter/categorical plot (no micrographs, spectra or schematics; no legend, no error bars, no printed data labels). The vertical axis is labelled "Cross-validation scores" and spans 0.2 to 1.4 in 0.2 increments with dashed horizontal gridlines; the horizontal axis is labelled "Numbers of Features" with integer ticks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and dashed vertical gridlines. Above each feature count sits a vertical column of filled light-blue circular markers representing every candidate feature-subset combination: five markers at 1 feature, about six at 2, about four at 3, three at 4 and a single marker at 5. The 1-feature column is by far the most dispersed, reaching from just above the 0.2 gridline up to just below the 1.3 level (between the 1.2 and 1.4 gridlines). Columns for 2-5 features are tightly clustered in the lower part of the axis, roughly between the 0.2 and 0.45 gridlines, with 2 features additionally containing one isolated marker near 0.7. The lowest marker of each column appears at 3 features. The figure demonstrates that adding features up to three collapses the scatter of cross-validation scores, whereas four and five features bring no further decrease.

observations.observation: The plot axes are labelled 'Cross-validation scores' (y, 0.2 to 1.4 with dashed gridlines at 0.2 intervals) and 'Numbers of Features' (x, ticks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5).

Each feature number is represented by a vertical column of filled light-blue circular markers: about five markers at 1 feature, about six at 2 features, about four at 3 features, three at 4 features and one at 5 features.
At 1 feature the markers are the most widely spread, spanning from just above the 0.2 gridline to a highest point lying between the 1.2 and 1.4 gridlines.
At 2 features one isolated marker sits near 0.7 while the remaining markers lie below the 0.45 gridline.
For 3, 4 and 5 features all markers are confined to a narrow band between roughly the 0.2 and 0.35 levels, i.e. the spread of cross-validation scores is strongly compressed relative to 1 feature.
No numeric data labels, legend, error bars or fitted line are printed; values can only be read approximately against the 0.2-spaced gridlines.
The caption states the figure presents 'Exhaustive screening results with different numbers of features'.
The citing text states minimum RMSE values of 0.341, 0.267, 0.257, 0.271 and 0.281 for 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 features respectively, indicating 3 features as the optimal prediction accuracy.

The citing text identifies the feature combination {δ_Ec, D_Ec, G} as giving the smallest RMSE value (0.257) within the 3-feature set, naming the local cohesive energy mismatch δ_EC, the cohesive energy difference D_EC and the shear modulus G as the key factors.

The y-axis is labelled 'Cross-validation scores' while the citing text reports the same set of minima as 'RMSE' values; the image itself does not print which metric the ordinate is, so the two readings are not reconciled by the pixels.

The single marker at 5 features lies lowest in its own column at approximately the 0.28 level, while the lowest marker overall appears in the 3-feature column, consistent with the cited minimum RMSE of 0.257 at 3 features.

subfigures.description: One scatter plot only: 'Cross-validation scores' (y, 0.2-1.4, step 0.2, dashed gridlines) versus 'Numbers of Features' (x, integer ticks 1-5). Light-blue circular markers form descending vertical stacks at each feature number; the stack is tallest/most dispersed at 1 feature and compresses to a narrow band near 0.25-0.35 for 3-5 features.
